stage_v1.name: wake_up
stage_v1.description: Basic hello world, encrypt a plain text read it back - decrypt and compare to input.

stage_v1.name: smoke
stage_v1.description: Encrypt a plain text read it back - decrypt and compare to input but use reference model to compare after both encryption and decryption.

stage_v1.name: csr_hw_reset
stage_v1.description: Verify the reset values as indicated in the RAL specification.
steps: Write all CSRs with a random value.
Apply reset to the DUT as well as the RAL model.
Read each CSR and compare it against the reset value.
Replicate this test for each reset that affects all or a subset of the CSRs.
Run this test for all available interfaces the CSRs are accessible from.
Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.

stage_v1.name: csr_rw
stage_v1.description: Verify accessibility of CSRs as indicated in the RAL specification.
steps: Loop through each CSR to write it with a random value.
Read the CSR back and check for correctness while adhering to its access policies.
Run this test for all available interfaces the CSRs are accessible from.
Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.

stage_v1.name: csr_bit_bash
stage_v1.description: Verify no aliasing within individual bits of a CSR.
steps: Walk a 1 through each CSR by flipping 1 bit at a time.
Read the CSR back and check for correctness while adhering to its access policies.
Verify that writing a specific bit within the CSR did not affect any of the other bits.
Run this test for all available interfaces the CSRs are accessible from.
Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.

stage_v1.name: csr_aliasing
stage_v1.description: Verify no aliasing within the CSR address space.
steps: Loop through each CSR to write it with a random value.
Shuffle and read ALL CSRs back.
Verify all CSRs except for the one that was written in this iteration should read back the previous value.
Check the written CSR for correctness while adhering to its access policies.
Run this test for all available interfaces the CSRs are accessible from.
Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.

stage_v1.name: csr_mem_rw_with_rand_reset
stage_v1.description: Verify random reset during CSR/memory access.
steps: Run csr_rw sequence to randomly access CSRs.
If memory exists, run mem_partial_access in parallel with csr_rw.
Randomly issue reset and then use hw_reset sequence to check all CSRs are reset to default value.
Run this test for all available interfaces the CSRs are accessible from.

stage_v1.name: regwen_csr_and_corresponding_lockable_csr
stage_v1.description: Verify regwen CSR and its corresponding lockable CSRs.
steps: Randomly access all CSRs.
Test when regwen CSR is set, its corresponding lockable CSRs become read-only registers.
notes: If regwen CSR is HW read-only, this feature can be fully tested by common CSR tests - csr_rw and csr_aliasing.
If regwen CSR is HW updated, a separate test should be created to test it.
This is only applicable if the block contains regwen and lockable CSRs.

stage_v2.name: algorithm
stage_v2.description: Compare cypher text from DUT with the output of a C model using same key and data.

stage_v2.name: key_length
stage_v2.description: Randomly select key length to verify all supported key lengths are working.

stage_v2.name: back2back
stage_v2.description: Back to back Messages are not possible as the DUT need to be idle before writing a new configuration. But Back2back verifies that DUT can handle back to back data blocks and other spacings.

stage_v2.name: backpressure
stage_v2.description: Try to write data to registers without offloading the DUT output to verify Stall functionality.

stage_v2.name: multi_message
stage_v2.description: Run multiple messages in a random mix of encryption / decryption. Each message should select its mode randomly.

stage_v2.name: failure_test
stage_v2.description: Tests what happens if a register is written at the wrong time? If a key does not match the key setting etc. Will the DUT ignore or fail gracefully.
examples: Enter a 256bit key but set DUT to use 128bit for encryption. Then enter the 128bit of the key and use for decryption. Will result match plain text and vice.
Write unsupported configurations (Key length and mode are 1 hot, what happens if more than one bit is set.)

stage_v2.name: trigger_clear_test
stage_v2.description: Exercise trigger and clear registers at random times to make sure we handle the different cornercases correctly.
stage_v2.example: Clearing data input or data output before the data is consumed or the DUT finishes an operation.

stage_v2.name: nist_test_vectors
stage_v2.description: Verify that the DUT handles the NIST test vectors correctly.

stage_v2.name: nist_test_vectors_gcm
stage_v2.description: Verify that the DUT handles the NIST GCM test vectors correctly.

stage_v2.name: reset_recovery
stage_v2.description: Pull reset at random times, make sure DUT recover/resets correctly and there is no residual data left in the registers.

stage_v2.name: stress
stage_v2.description: This will combine the other individual testpoints to ensure we stress test everything across the board.

stage_v2.name: sideload
stage_v2.description: Verify that DUT uses sideload correctly when sideload is enabled and that it ignores any valid on the bus when disabled.

stage_v2.name: deinitialization
stage_v2.description: Make sure that there is no residual data from latest operation.

stage_v2.name: stress_all
stage_v2.description: Run assorted sequences back-to-back.

stage_v2.name: gcm_save_and_restore
stage_v2.description: Verify that saving and restoring contexts in GCM works correctly. When triggered, save the current context, clear the entire state, restore the context, and proceed with the operation.

stage_v2.name: alert_test
stage_v2.description: Verify common alert_test CSR that allows SW to mock-inject alert requests.
steps: Enable a random set of alert requests by writing random value to alert_test CSR.
Check each alert_tx.alert_p pin to verify that only the requested alerts are triggered.

During alert_handshakes, write alert_test CSR again to verify that: If alert_test writes to current ongoing alert handshake, the alert_test request will be ignored. If alert_test writes to current idle alert handshake, a new alert_handshake should be triggered.
Wait for the alert handshakes to finish and verify alert_tx.alert_p pins all sets back to 0.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2.name: tl_d_oob_addr_access
stage_v2.description: Access out of bounds address and verify correctness of response / behavior.

stage_v2.name: tl_d_illegal_access
stage_v2.description: Drive unsupported requests via TL interface and verify correctness of response / behavior.
tlul_protocol_errors: Some mask bits not set when opcode is PutFullData
Mask does not match the transfer size (e.g. a_address = 0x00, a_size = 0, a_mask = 'b0010)
Mask and address misaligned (e.g. a_address = 0x01, a_mask = 'b0001)
Address and size aren't aligned (e.g. a_address = 0x01, a_size != 0)
opentitan_errors: Write a CSR with unaligned address (e.g. a_address[1:0] != 0)
Write a CSR less than its width (e.g. when CSR is 2 bytes wide, only write 1 byte)
Write a memory with a_mask != '1 when it doesn't support partial accesses

stage_v2.name: tl_d_outstanding_access
stage_v2.description: Drive back-to-back requests without waiting for response to ensure there is one transaction outstanding within the TL device. Also, verify one outstanding when back-to-back accesses are made to the same address.

stage_v2.name: tl_d_partial_access
stage_v2.description: Access CSR with one or more bytes of data. For read, expect to return all word value of the CSR. For write, enabling bytes should cover all CSR valid fields.

stage_v2s.name: reseeding
stage_v2s.description: Verify that internal PRNGs are effectively reseeded upon manually triggering a PRNG reseed, and - depending on the configuration - if the initial key changes.

stage_v2s.name: fault_inject
stage_v2s.description: Verify that injecting bit errors in one of the state machines or the round counter triggers an error.

stage_v2s.name: shadow_reg_update_error
steps: Randomly pick a shadowed register in the DUT.
Write it twice with different values.
Verify that the update error alert is triggered and the register value remains unchanged.
Verify the update_error status register field is set to 1.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2s.name: shadow_reg_read_clear_staged_value
stage_v2s.description: Verify reading a shadowed register will clear its staged value.
steps: Randomly pick a shadowed register in the DUT.
Write it once and read it back to clear the staged value.
Then write it twice with the same new value (but different from the previous step).
Read it back to verify the new value and ensure that the update error alert did not trigger.
Verify the update_error status register field remains the same value.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2s.name: shadow_reg_storage_error
steps: Randomly pick a shadowed register in the DUT.
Backdoor write to shadowed or committed flops to create a storage fatal alert.
Check if fatal alert continuously fires until reset.
Verify that all other frontdoor write attempts are blocked during the storage error.
Verify that storage_error status register field is set to 1.
Reset the DUT.
Read all CSRs to ensure the DUT is properly reset.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2s.name: shadowed_reset_glitch
stage_v2s.description: Verify toggle shadowed_rst_n pin can trigger storage error.
steps: Randomly drive shadowed_rst_n pin to low or rst_n pin to low.
Check if any registers have been written before the reset. If so check if storage error fatal alert is triggered.
Check status register.
Drive shadowed_rst_n pin or rst_n pin back to high.
If fatal alert is triggered, reset the DUT.
Read all CSRs to ensure the DUT is properly reset.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2s.name: shadow_reg_update_error_with_csr_rw
stage_v2s.description: Run shadow_reg_update_error sequence in parallel with csr_rw sequence.
steps: Randomly select one of the above sequences.
Apply csr_rw sequence in parallel but disable the csr_access_abort to ensure all shadowed registers' write/read to be executed without aborting.
Repeat the above steps a bunch of times.

stage_v2s.name: tl_intg_err
stage_v2s.description: Verify that the data integrity check violation generates an alert.
steps: Randomly inject errors on the control, data, or the ECC bits during CSR accesses. Verify that triggers the correct fatal alert.
Inject a fault at the onehot check in u_reg.u_prim_reg_we_check and verify the corresponding fatal alert occurs.

stage_v2s.name: sec_cm_lc_escalate_en_intersig_mubi
stage_v2s.description: Verify the countermeasure(s) LC_ESCALATE_EN.INTERSIG.MUBI. Upon randomly switching the life cycle escalation input signal, it is ensured that the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.

stage_v3.name: stress_all_with_rand_reset
stage_v3.description: This test runs 3 parallel threads - stress_all, tl_errors and random reset. After reset is asserted, the test will read and check all valid CSR registers.
